stem: A biological-control release was followed by fewer pest detections, but scouting effort was also reduced and a sanitation change occurred at the same time. What should the follow-up report say?
choices: Record the improvement but identify the sampling change and overlapping sanitation action as confounders, then define a comparable next monitoring round.
Attribute the improvement entirely to the biological control because it occurred first.
Ignore the sanitation change because it was not a pesticide treatment.
Remove the earlier scouting method from the record so all rounds appear comparable.
rationale: Treatment follow-up should compare against baseline while preserving confounders and method changes; correlation alone does not establish the sole cause of improvement.
